Parabolic 1.1.1 for Android fixes `zipimport.ZipImportError: bad local file header`, an error that could stop a link lookup (**Bilgileri getir**) or a download, most often right after the app was opened. Both Android builds get the fix: the regular one and the `legacy` one for Android 11 and older. The iOS app only gets the new version number; it unpacks yt-dlp into a folder and was never affected.

---

## What went wrong

On Android, yt-dlp is a single zip archive that Python runs directly. Python reads the archive's table of contents once, when yt-dlp starts, and then opens the file again by name each time it loads more of yt-dlp's code. yt-dlp loads the code for a site only when it looks up a link from that site, so this happens in the middle of every run.

The daily automatic yt-dlp update starts when the app is opened. When it finished while a lookup or a download was running, the new yt-dlp replaced the old one on disk, and the running yt-dlp then looked for its code at the old version's positions in the new file. Python stopped with "bad local file header". Opening the app and looking a link up straight away was enough to run into it, and with the nightly channel there is a new yt-dlp almost every day.

## The fix

A downloaded yt-dlp update is now put in place only while no yt-dlp is running: at once if nothing is running, otherwise as soon as the last lookup or download has finished. It is still checked against GitHub's SHA-256 first, as in 1.1.0. If you update by hand in **Ayarlar** while something is downloading, the message says that the new version will be installed when the running work has finished. An update waiting this way is kept when the app is closed and is installed the next time yt-dlp starts.

If you saw the error in 1.1.0, nothing on the phone is damaged: looking the link up again after the update has finished works.
